Grey and white terrazzo floor with brass divider strips, worn dull along the path to the counter. Four rows of moulded mustard-yellow fibreglass chairs bolted to steel beams, one chair cracked. At the far end a long brown wood-veneer counter with six service windows of reeded frosted glass, each with a small round speaking grille and a slot for papers, and a small mechanical number box above each window. High on the end wall a large mechanical split-flap "now serving" board. A red ticket dispenser on a chrome pole near the entrance. A rubber plant in a pot, half dead. A plain wall clock. Tall steel-framed windows on the left with yellowed net curtains. Ceiling of fluorescent tube fittings, two tubes dead. Nearly empty: an old man asleep upright in the third row, a woman knitting at the end of a row.

Photographic qualities: available light only, flat overcast daylight from the windows mixed with greenish fluorescent light, low contrast, soft shadows, deep focus so the whole room is sharp, slight lens vignetting, fine film grain, muted desaturated colour. A real location that has been used every day for decades: dust, wear, mismatched repairs. Shot on an ARRI Alexa with a 32 mm prime. The deadpan tableau framing of Roy Andersson.

Avoid: readable text, signage or logos anywhere; LED screens; blue government signage; glossy or polished surfaces; god rays, haze or dramatic light; rim light; shallow depth of field or bokeh; teal-and-orange grade; HDR look; anything new or clean.
